title: C Programming
description: Get close to the machine: structs, pointers, manual memory management, and build your own garbage collector from scratch.

lessons.title: C Basics
lessons.content:
# C Basics

C is a compiled, statically-typed language from 1972 that still powers operating systems, databases, and language runtimes today. Learning C means learning how a computer actually works, no hidden garbage collector, no implicit conversions you didn't ask for, just you and the machine.

## Your first program

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    printf("Hello, Kodstigen!\n");
    return 0;
}
```

- `#include <stdio.h>` pulls in the standard I/O library, so `printf` exists.
- `int main(void)` is the entry point every C program starts from, it returns an `int` **exit code** to the operating system, `0` means "success".
- `printf` formats and prints text, `\n` is a newline escape sequence, unlike Python there's no automatic newline after a print.

## Compiling and running

C is compiled ahead of time, there's no interpreter:

```bash
gcc hello.c -o hello
./hello
```

`gcc` translates your `.c` source file into a native executable, `-o hello` names the output file. Every time you change the source, you recompile before running again.

## Variables and types

Unlike Python or JavaScript, every variable in C has a fixed, explicit type:

```c
int xp = 0;
float ratio = 0.5f;
char grade = 'A';
xp += 10;
```

There's no `var`/`let` inference, you declare the type up front and it never changes. This is why C is fast, the compiler knows exactly how much memory each variable needs and never has to check types at runtime.

> [!TIP]
> C has no built-in string type, a "string" is really just an array of `char` ending in a special `\0` (null terminator) byte. You'll see why that matters a lot once we get to pointers.

questions.prompt: What does main() returning 0 signal to the operating system?
options: Nothing, the return value is ignored

questions.prompt: In C, a variable's type must be declared up front and cannot change later.
The command to compile hello.c into an executable called hello with gcc is: gcc hello.c -o ____

lessons.title: Structs

questions.prompt: How are a struct's members arranged in memory?
options: Randomly, wherever there is free space
Each member gets its own separate heap allocation
They are not stored, only computed on access

questions.prompt: typedef creates a shorter alias for a type, like naming an anonymous struct Point instead of writing struct Point every time.
Given "struct Point p;", you access its x member with the ____ operator: p.x

lessons.title: Pointers

questions.prompt: What does the & operator do when applied to a variable?
Passing a pointer to a function lets that function modify the caller's original variable.
Given "int *p = &x;", the ____ operator (*p) reads or writes the value p points to.

lessons.title: Enums

questions.prompt: By default, what integer value does the first member of an enum get?
You can explicitly assign a specific integer value to an enum member, like OK = 200.
Under the hood, an enum value in C is really just an ____.

lessons.title: Unions

questions.prompt: What is the size of a C union roughly equal to?
options: The sum of all its members
The size of its largest member
The size of its first member only
questions.answer: The size of its largest member

questions.prompt: A C union's members occupy separate, non-overlapping memory, similar to a struct.
Pairing a union with an enum "tag" field to remember which member is currently valid is called a ____ union.

lessons.title: Stack and Heap

questions.prompt: Which memory region is automatically reclaimed the instant a function returns?
Memory allocated with malloc() must be freed manually with free(), it is not reclaimed automatically.
Forgetting to free heap memory that is no longer used is called a memory ____.

lessons.title: Advanced Pointers

questions.prompt: Why would a function take an int** (pointer to a pointer) parameter?
options: To make the code look more advanced
To modify which address the caller's own pointer holds
It is required for all malloc calls
questions.answer: To modify which address the caller's own pointer holds

questions.prompt: For an int pointer p, the expression (p + 1) advances by exactly 1 byte, regardless of type.
In most expressions, an array name automatically ____ into a pointer to its first element.

lessons.title: Stack Data Structure

questions.prompt: What does the -> operator do?
options: Dereferences a pointer and accesses a member in one step
questions.answer: Dereferences a pointer and accesses a member in one step

questions.prompt: In the IntStack example, freeing the struct before freeing its items array would leak the array's memory.
A stack follows a "last in, first ____" ordering.

lessons.title: Objects

questions.prompt: In the Obj struct, what determines which member of the "as" union is currently valid?
options: The order the struct was declared in

questions.prompt: Every Obj in this design is heap-allocated so it can be shared and outlive the function that created it.
Combining a type tag with a union to represent any kind of value is called a tagged ____.

lessons.title: Refcounting GC

questions.prompt: In reference counting, when is an object freed?
options: When its reference count reaches zero
Whenever malloc runs low on memory
questions.answer: When its reference count reaches zero

questions.prompt: Reference counting correctly frees two objects that reference each other in a cycle, even if nothing else references them.
Two objects that reference each other so their counts never reach zero form a reference ____.

lessons.title: Mark and Sweep GC

questions.prompt: What are the two phases of a mark-and-sweep collector?
Mark-and-sweep correctly frees a reference cycle that nothing external points to, unlike plain refcounting.
The starting points a mark-and-sweep collector walks from (globals, the current stack) are called ____.
